sources.title: Boise-area rock climbing gym owner says it will remain open | Idaho Statesman
sources.content: Asana has been an indoor climbing spot for the Treasure Valley at 4977 N. Glenwood St. since 2017. In June, the gym’s owner, Jamey Sproull, sent out the dreaded message to its climbers notifying them of the pending closure in November of this year. According to the message, Asana had “not been offered a new long-term lease agreement.” On Friday, Sproull sent out the good news in a message “I never thought I would be able to write.” According to the message, the property manager expressed a commitment to keeping Asana open at the current location. But there still are kinks to work out, Sproull said. A long-term lease agreement is not finalized yet, but Sproull stated that they have “every reason to believe” Asana will continue to operate at the location. [...] “When I announced that the gym would be closing, I did so because that was the reality we were facing,” Sproull stated in the message. “We had no long-term lease, no viable path to remain in the building, and no realistic alternative location that could support a climbing gym. It was one of the hardest announcements I have ever had to make.” Sproull said Asana will continue its regular operations and invest in the gym’s programs, youth climbing, competitions and events. He noted that the gym still has work to do as the agreement is finalized and will share updates. The “strength” of the climbing community helped Asana push through the weeks following the closure announcement, Sproull stated in the message. He thanked the gym’s members, staff, volunteers and the property manager. [...] The property is owned by TPC Glenwood, LLC, an affiliate of a developer and property manager that oversees businesses and housing in the Treasure Valley and across the western U.S. According to the closure message, the gym’s lease was originally set to expire at the end of June, but the property managers granted Asana an extension on the lease through the end of the year. Asana’s new gym opened in January. Asana’s new gym opened in January. Courtesy of Asana When Asana faced with the possibility of an end at the current location, Sproull said he looked for a new location, but niche zoning, the building height needed for a viable climbing gym and the high lease rates made the search nearly impossible.
